title: Usage Sag-Band Pricing Probe for Bidirectional Streaming
creator: Priya Kapoor
description: Objective: Validate a layered per-token pricing approach that decouples input vs output token rates for streaming calls and introduces a small "sag-band" (grace credits and smoothing) for low-volume streaming customers to reduce churn while protecting unit economics. This probe combines three levers: asymmetric input/output rates, a streaming session surcharge for very long-lived idle connections, and a monthly minimum smoothing band ("sag-band") that credits customers for short-term burstiness.
comments: 2026-02-15 Priya: Drafted hypothesis and initial metrics. Hypothesis: modestly increasing output-token price (by 10-25% in treatment arms) will preserve revenue for high-output workflows (chat assistants, summarization) while applying a small sag-band credit will reduce short-term churn for low-volume users who suffer from billing noise.
2026-02-18 Finance review (J. Lee): Concern about visibility. Requested per-customer PnL sims by cohort (small, mid, enterprise). Assigned ENG to export cohorted token histograms.

2026-02-22 Engineering (Asha Patel): Added telemetry acceptance criteria: must emit token_direction (ingress|egress), session_id for streaming, idle_ms buckets. Provided draft schema and example events.

2026-02-25 Legal (E. Chen): Flagged contract language required for 'minimum billing floor' and streaming surcharge. Legal requested a short Q&A doc for the security questionnaire clarifying how streaming sessions are identified, what metadata we collect, and how billing data maps to logs.

2026-03-01 PM sync: Decided on two treatment arms: T1 = Output tokens +15% rate, streaming session surcharge removed but sag-band credits applied; T2 = Output tokens +20% rate + streaming session surcharge of $0.002 per idle-minute above 30m, sag-band credits applied. Control = current symmetric input/output per-token pricing. Run length: 6 weeks rollout to new accounts and 10% randomized sample of existing self-serve accounts (excludes committed enterprise).

2026-03-05 Data (R. Singh): Uploaded simulation spreadsheet with cohort-level revenue and cost projections for both treatments (link below). Preliminary sims show T1 improves revenue +6% on aggregate with <1% uplift in churn; T2 improves revenue +9% but risk increases for low-volume tools (chatbots) without sag-band tuning.
2026-03-08 Design (L. Park): Drafted billing UI changes to surface per-route input/output breakdown and 'sag-band credit' line item; prototype link attached.
2026-03-10 PM decision: Proceed with T1 and canary T2 on a small pilot if safeguards (auto-refund window, explicit invoices) pass finance and legal reviews. Action items assigned.

Next steps: implement metering changes (ENG-20401), billing engine rules (ENG-20710), update pricing docs and SDKs, prepare communications for self-serve customers, and run security questionnaire updates for enterprise PRDs.
